framework: connexion/Flask (OpenAPI server, plus a parallel KG2 variant) + Tornado (autocomplete service); sqlite3 raw-SQL data layer, SQLAlchemy ORM for tracker/cache
model_context: LLM labeling performed inline by the Claude Code session model (glm-5.3). No external LLM API was invoked; the agent itself is the labeling model. Determinism guardrails: fixed confidence values, rule-consistent rationales, one decision per CSV row in a single pass per batch (no re-ask was needed - no JSON decode failures since decisions were rendered deterministically from the reviewed code evidence).
labeling_inputs: source code under dataset/codeql_databases/sql_injection_dbs/rtx_vuln (read-only review: autocomplete/server.py, autocomplete/rtxcomplete.py, autocomplete/create_load_db.py, UI/OpenAPI controllers (query/asyncquery/translate/entity/response/status/pubmed_mesh_ngd/meta_knowledge_graph + KG2 variants), ARAX/ARAXQuery/ARAX_query.py, ARAX_query_tracker.py, ARAX_decorator.py, Overlay/predictor/predictor.py, Overlay/fisher_exact_test.py, Overlay/compute_ngd.py, Overlay/overlay_clinical_info.py, Overlay/ngd/build_ngd_database.py, Overlay/GraphSage_train/py_scripts/*, NodeSynonymizer/node_synonymizer.py, KnowledgeSources/COHD_local/scripts/COHDIndex.py, ResponseCache/response_cache.py, kg2c/create_kg2c_files.py, kg2c/record_kg2c_meta_info.py, reasoningtool/kg-construction/KGNodeIndex.py, reasoningtool/kg-construction/NormGoogleDistance.py)
references_not_loaded: augur-0.3.0/references/django.md, fastapi.md and all other framework references: no django/fastapi usage (detection.json confidence 0.0 for Django); tornado has no reference file; flask.md was loaded for the connexion/Flask front-end.

batches.scope: OpenAPI front-end (connexion controllers incl. the KG2 variant, ARAX_query_tracker)
ARAX pipeline data layer (node_synonymizer, ARAX_decorator, predictor, fisher_exact_test, compute_ngd, ARAX_query)
COHD local index (COHDIndex.py sources and sinks)
offline CLI/ETL/build scripts (kg2c, KGNodeIndex, GraphSage py_scripts, ngd build, reasoningtool, NLPCode) + code-evidence sanitizer entries

src_ns_access_param_bound.rationale: Internal NodeSynonymizer access-method parameter (not an external boundary); the value only reaches sqlite3 lookups as bound `?` parameters (node_synonymizer.py:1747-1861, 2107-2138), never SQL text.

src_header_no_sql.rationale: Genuine HTTP header boundary (x-forwarded-for read in the query/asyncquery controllers), but the value is attached to the query dict as remote_address and persisted only through the SQLAlchemy ORM with bound parameters (ARAX_query_tracker.py:260-270); it never enters SQL text.
evidence: ARAX_query_tracker.py:260-270: session.add(ARAXQuery(...)) - ORM insert, bound values

src_cli_offline.rationale: CLI argument of an offline reasoning/ETL/build script (no network surface); operator-controlled, matching detection.json's cli_env exclusion. These scripts feed only static or parameterized ETL SQL; not an attacker-influenced boundary for CWE-89.

src_env_config.rationale: Environment/config value read at startup (RTXConfiguration or server status); deployment-controlled, not attacker input, and not part of any SQL text construction.

src_internal_comprehension.rationale: Internal comprehension/lambda iteration parameter over database or API results inside COHDIndex; not an input boundary and carries no external data into SQL text.

src_mode_no_sql.rationale: HTTP query parameter of GET /status/logs, but mode only selects the log-reading path (status_controller.py:45-50; ARAX_query_tracker.get_logs reads a file) - no SQL execution is reachable from it.
evidence: status_controller.py:45-49: mode == 'env' -> str(os.environ); else get_logs(mode) reads the /tmp log file

src_mode_flag.rationale: Control flag of the ARAX pipeline entry (stream/asynchronous mode selection); not data that reaches SQL.

sum_arax_pipeline_entry.rationale: Pipeline propagation step: the user query dict from POST /query and /asyncquery enters ARAXQuery.query_return_message/query_return_stream here; its qnode ids, curies and categories propagate into NodeSynonymizer, predictor, fisher_exact_test, ARAXDecorator and COHD SQL construction. A summary step is needed so controller-level taint survives into the overlay/data-access layers.
evidence: ARAX_query.py:100/216: pipeline entry invoked from query_controller.py:62/72 and asyncquery_controller.py:34
detection.json propagation_notes: user query_dict -> ActionsParser -> add_qnode/expand/overlay -> SQL builders

sum_canonical_curies_hub.rationale: Canonicalization hub on the attacker-curie path (get_canonical_curies/get_equivalent_nodes build quote-escaped IN lists executed at node_synonymizer.py:1987/2048); a summary step propagates controller taint into this hub.
evidence: node_synonymizer.py:1929-1960: curies upper-cased, quote-doubled, joined into IN-list
node_synonymizer.py:1967-1987: f-string sql executed at cursor.execute(sql)

src_cohd_helper_param.rationale: Internal helper parameter (curie canonicalization for the COHD mapping); the value only reaches NodeSynonymizer bound/escaped lookups.

src_cohd_api_param.rationale: Parameter forwarded to the remote cohd.io REST API via requests.post (COHDIndex.py:310/329); no local SQL execution consumes this value.
evidence: COHDIndex.py:411-428: get_concept_ids builds a query dict and calls _call_cohd_biolink_to_omop_api

src_status_no_sql.rationale: HTTP query parameters of GET /status, but the values only reach SQLAlchemy ORM filters, the :n named bind parameter of ARAX_query_tracker.get_entries, or os.kill (terminate_job); none enter SQL text.

src_responsecache_orm.rationale: HTTP parameter of GET/POST /response, but ResponseCache accesses storage exclusively through the SQLAlchemy ORM (session.query/filter/add with bound values); no raw SQL text.
evidence: response_cache.py:250 get_response and :491 store_callback use session.query/session.add only

src_cohd_domain_const.rationale: domain is interpolated unescaped into COHD SQL (e.g. COHDIndex.py:1186 "c.domain_id = '{domain}'"), but every current caller passes hardcoded constants ('Drug'/'Procedure'/empty string) from the offline CLI or commented-out code - no external input reaches it. Retained as hardening evidence, not a live source.

src_cohd_reformat_helper.rationale: String-reformatting helper for CURIE vocabularies (ICD-10/SNOMED renames); no SQL construction and no external boundary.

src_cohd_cli_typed_params.rationale: OMOP concept identifiers guarded by isinstance int/list checks and (for dataset_id) a 1/2/3 whitelist; in the current call graph they originate from the offline CLI (COHDIndex.py:3127+) or the trusted cohd.io mapping API, never from HTTP input. The downstream tuple-repr interpolation is fragile but unreachable from an attacker in this snapshot.
evidence: overlay_clinical_info.py:176-178: the only live ARAX caller passes API-mapped pair strings

src_entity_bound.rationale: Genuine HTTP boundary (GET/POST /entity), but q/body flow into NodeSynonymizer.get_normalizer_results whose SQL is fully bound-parameter (node_synonymizer.py:2107-2138).

src_query_body_tp.rationale: Primary attacker-controlled input: the POST /query and /asyncquery JSON body (also read via connexion.request.get_json()). The query dict drives the ARAX pipeline whose node curies and categories reach raw-SQL text: predictor.py:65/328-372 (unescaped f-strings) and fisher_exact_test.py:579 (unescaped category interpolation). A complete external-source-to-SQL-text data flow exists.
evidence: predictor.py:65: f"select * from GRAPH where curie='{curie_name}'"

src_translate_disabled.rationale: POST /translate is disabled - it returns 501 without processing (translate_controller.py:25); the request body never reaches any data layer.

src_ngd_no_sql.rationale: HTTP query parameters of GET /pubmed_mesh_ngd, but term1/term2 flow into NormGoogleDistance.api_ngd which only performs NCBI E-utilities/MeSH HTTP lookups (NormGoogleDistance.py:218-239); no SQL execution.

src_control_flag.rationale: Control/configuration flag: kg_name is validated to KG1/KG2 with the table prefix then hardcoded (node_synonymizer.py:1734-1740), and return_all_categories/return_type are booleans; never attacker data in SQL text.
evidence: node_synonymizer.py:1734-1740: kg_prefix validated then forced to 'kg2'

sum_normalizer_bound.rationale: Propagation param for the /entity endpoints; entities reach only bound-parameter lookups (node_synonymizer.py:2107-2138, 2267). Summary retained for pipeline completeness; classified fp because the channel is parameterized.

src_tornado_path_unused.rationale: Tornado path-capture parameter (arg captured by /auto(.*)-style routes) is never used in the handler bodies; the live inputs are get_argument values (server.py:24-116).

src_tornado_word_shadowed.rationale: The word=None path parameter is immediately overwritten by self.get_argument('word') in every autocomplete handler; the path-captured value never reaches data access (server.py:28/49/75/102).

sum_get_nodes_like.rationale: Live propagation step on the /nodeslike HTTP path: word and requested_limit from get_argument flow into get_nodes_like, whose SQL at rtxcomplete.py:49/76/88/112 interpolates word unescaped and requested_limit after an int() cast. Summary step connects server.py:101-104 to the sqlite sink.

src_signal_param.rationale: OS signal-handler arguments (SIGPIPE number/frame); not attacker input and unrelated to SQL.

sum_ngd_quote_filtered.rationale: Pipeline param carrying canonicalized curies into compute_ngd.load_curie_to_pmids_data; the SQL builder excludes any curie containing a single quote (compute_ngd.py:346), so the IN-list interpolation cannot break the string literal.
evidence: compute_ngd.py:346: [f"'{curie}'" for curie in chunk if "'" not in curie]

src_meta_kg_no_sql.rationale: HTTP query parameter of /meta_knowledge_graph; it selects an output format in static metadata assembly (KnowledgeSourceMetadata); no SQL text construction.

sum_query_dict_fork.rationale: Fork/pipe plumbing that carries the user query dict from the connexion controller into the ARAXQuery child process (query_controller.py:23-58, 61-72); a summary step is needed so taint crosses the process boundary into pipeline SQL sinks.
evidence: query_controller.py:43: query_runner(query_dict) inside the forked child

src_callable_param.rationale: Callable (function object) parameter, not data; no taint semantics for CWE-89.

src_tornado_getarg_tp.rationale: Attacker-controlled HTTP query parameters of GET /nodeslike (limit/word/callback at server.py:101-103) flowing directly into rtxcomplete.get_nodes_like's unescaped f-string SQL - a complete external source-to-SQL-text flow.

src_tornado_getarg_dead.rationale: Real HTTP query parameters of /auto, /fuzzy, /autofuzzy, but rtxcomplete.prefix/fuzzy/autofuzzy are not defined in the current snapshot (only load() and get_nodes_like() exist), so those handlers fail with AttributeError before any SQL; retained as boundary evidence.
evidence: rtxcomplete.py:20-135: only load() and get_nodes_like() defined

sink_predictor_curie_unescaped.rationale: Unescaped f-string SQL: f"select * from GRAPH where curie='{curie_name}'" - no quoting or escaping of any kind (predictor.py:65). curie_name arrives from the ARAX query pipeline (Overlay/DTD curies that fall back to the raw user-supplied curie when the NodeSynonymizer has no canonical form), so HTTP input can reach the SQL text.
evidence: DTD_querier.py:337-414: normalizer preferred_curie passed into the DTD db lookups

sink_predictor_dtd_unescaped.rationale: DTD probability lookups interpolate disease/drug curies (or whole lists via tuple repr) into f-string SQL without escaping (predictor.py:328/348/350/370/372); values come from normalizer preferred curies that fall back to raw user curies. Candidate true path from POST /query.
evidence: predictor.py:328: f"... where disease = '{disease}' and drug = '{drug}'"

sink_ngd_quote_excluded.rationale: IN-list SQL over canonicalized curies, but the builder drops every curie containing a single quote (compute_ngd.py:346), which makes breaking out of the single-quoted literal impossible; values are canonicalized pipeline curies.

sink_kgnodeindex_bound_or_static.rationale: Offline CLI KG-index build/lookup tool; the SQL text is static DDL (KGNodeIndex.py:94-98, 277-279) or parameterized `?` lookups over a hardcoded table name; all values are bound (KGNodeIndex.py:247-258, 289-520).

sink_static_ddl.rationale: Static CREATE/DROP/INDEX DDL executed by offline database build paths; no external data in the SQL text.

sink_etl_static_bound.rationale: Offline ETL/build script; the SQL is static literals and executemany INSERTs with `?` bound row values; no attacker-reachable input.

sink_kg2c_etl_bound.rationale: kg2c build script; the f-strings interpolate only the static PROPERTIES_LOOKUP column lists and generated schema fragments, while row values are bound via `?` (create_kg2c_files.py:389-414).
evidence: create_kg2c_files.py:390-395: question_marks_string + executemany with bound values

sink_fisher_escaped.rationale: IN-list SQL over canonicalized curies escaped with .replace("'", "''") (fisher_exact_test.py:456) - correct SQLite single-quote doubling; the string-literal context cannot be broken.

sink_fisher_category_unescaped.rationale: f"SELECT C.count FROM category_counts WHERE C.category = '{node_type}'" with no escaping (fisher_exact_test.py:575-579); node_type derives from the user's query-graph node categories (fisher_exact_test.py:102 -> :331 -> size_of_given_type_in_KP) and convert_string_to_snake_case/convert_string_biolinkformat only re-case the string - they are not a whitelist (fisher_exact_test.py:617-650). An attacker-controlled string can reach SQL text via POST /query.

sink_rtxcomplete_word_unescaped.rationale: Autocomplete sqlite lookups interpolate the raw HTTP word parameter (and derived floor/ceiling/word_part) into double-quoted SQL string literals with no escaping (rtxcomplete.py:49/76/88; %-format at :112). A word containing a double quote breaks the literal - a direct, fully attacker-controlled SQL injection on GET /nodeslike.

sink_bound_insert.rationale: INSERT with `?` bound parameters (rtxcomplete.py:106/127); values never enter SQL text.

sink_decorator_escaped.rationale: KG2c sqlite IN-list SQL whose node/search keys are first quote-doubled (ARAX_decorator.py:67/149: .replace("'", "''")); the correct escape for the single-quoted string-literal context; keys are query-derived but neutralized.

sink_cohd_pair_second_order.rationale: concept_pair_id IN-list/'=' SQL interpolates pair strings unescaped (COHDIndex.py:983-1053), but the only live caller (overlay_clinical_info.py:176-178) passes 'omop1_omop2' strings produced by the trusted cohd.io mapping API from user curies - a second-order channel that currently yields numeric strings. Human review needed: confirm cohd.io cannot return crafted identifiers; parameterization recommended.

sink_cohd_static_literal.rationale: Static literal SQL (count/select-all) in the COHD local database scripts; no interpolation of external data.

sink_cohd_cli_typed.rationale: Unescaped f-string SQL over concept_id/dataset_id/domain, but scalar strings are rejected by isinstance(int/list) guards, dataset_id is whitelisted to 1/2/3, and current callers are the offline CLI (COHDIndex.py:3127+) and ETL scripts passing constants. Not attacker-reachable in this snapshot; flagged for hardening.
evidence: COHDIndex.py:480-491/550-558/1088-1104: type guards and dataset_id whitelist

sink_ns_inlist_escaped.rationale: IN-list SQL over user-influenced curies/names, but the values are first passed through re.sub("'", "''") quote-doubling (node_synonymizer.py:1608/1931/1952/2038), the correct escape for SQLite single-quoted literals; reachable from the HTTP pipeline yet neutralized.

sink_ns_bound_fstring.rationale: f-string SQL interpolates only the static table prefix/TESTSUFFIX; the user value is passed as a bound `?` parameter (node_synonymizer.py:1747-1861, 2107-2320).

sink_ns_executemany_bound.rationale: Bulk INSERT executemany with static SQL text and `?` bound row values (node_synonymizer.py:432-505, offline database build path).

sink_slim_etl.rationale: GraphSage slim-database ETL script; the f-strings interpolate ETL-derived curie lists or generated schema strings from a local DSL input file in an offline script; no HTTP boundary (generate_slim_databases.py:448-604).
evidence: generate_slim_databases.py:501-507: ETL curie list -> tuple interpolation in an offline script

sink_sqlalchemy_text_bound.rationale: sqlalchemy.text() receives a static SQL fragment; the user-controlled last_n_hours is bound via the :n named parameter with .params() (ARAX_query_tracker.py:283-291) - a fully parameterized channel, not a raw-SQL sink for CWE-89.

san_int_cast.rationale: requested_limit is cast with int() before interpolation into the LIMIT clause (rtxcomplete.py:34 -> :49); non-numeric input raises before SQL execution, neutralizing the limit channel of the /nodeslike sink (the word channel remains injectable).

san_quote_doubling_ns.rationale: re.sub("'", "''") quote-doubling applied to curies/names before IN-list construction (node_synonymizer.py:1931; the same pattern at :1608, :1952, :2038); correct escaping for SQLite single-quoted string literals; guards the sinks at :1618/:1987/:2048. Only the string-literal context is protected, which is adequate here because the IN-list is the sole interpolation.

san_quote_doubling_decorator.rationale: node_key/search_key .replace("'", "''") before IN-list SQL (ARAX_decorator.py:67 and :149); correct SQLite string-literal escape guarding the execute calls at :72/:154.

san_quote_doubling_fisher.rationale: curie_id .replace("'", "''") applied to canonicalized curies before the neighbor-count IN-list SQL (fisher_exact_test.py:456; restored at :470), guarding the execute at :468.

san_quote_exclusion.rationale: The curie_to_pmids IN-list builder drops every curie containing a single quote, so only quote-free values are interpolated into single-quoted literals (compute_ngd.py:346); the string-literal context of the execute at :347 cannot be broken.
evidence: compute_ngd.py:346: [f"'{curie}'" for curie in chunk if "'" not in curie]

san_dataset_whitelist.rationale: dataset_id is restricted to the whitelist {1, 2, 3} before any SQL interpolation (representative guard at COHDIndex.py:550-558; the same pattern guards every COHD query method, e.g. :864-872, :1096-1104, :1174-1182). Values outside the whitelist are rejected before the f-string SQL is reached.
evidence: COHDIndex.py:550-558: dataset_id == 1 or 2 or 3 else return []

san_named_bind.rationale: Named-bind channel: the user-controlled last_n_hours is supplied via .params(n=last_n_hours) for the static text() fragments (ARAX_query_tracker.py:283-291); the value never enters SQL text.
